survey: A pair of flip-flops lying flat side by side, seen from above at an angle with the toe ends toward the lower left. Each has one flat, rounded-oblong orange sole with a raised rim and a field of round dimples at the toe end. Each yellow strap is a V shape. Its point drops into a thin toe post, which goes into a hole in the sole near the toe end. Its two arms run back and outward to the sole edges and go into small slots about halfway along the sole, which is how a real flip-flop is built. Both soles rest flat on the same plane. The tool panel marks no thin-part ends or branches, so no part is left loose. The two flip-flops are near copies of each other rather than a mirrored left and right pair. Since the soles are drawn almost symmetric, that is an acceptable simplification and not a construction fault.
